basis: All five evidence commands re-run and print what the finding quotes. I re-derived the central claim by the inverse route the finding did not take: instead of counting GetDailySpend consumers, I asked who ever WRITES the two fields. `git grep -nE '\b(CapCents|FillRatePct)\b' -- 'internal/**/*.go' 'cmd/**/*.go'` returns no assignment to inventory.DailySpend.CapCents or .FillRatePct anywhere in the repository, test code included. The only hits that assign are internal/adapters/httpserver/handlers/campaigns_analytics.go:97, which fills the handler's own local fillRateRow struct, and internal/domain/portfolio/analysis.go:207, which is a different type (portfolio.analysis_types.go:66, a same-name collision the finding correctly did not cite). So both fields are structurally guaranteed zero on every value that crosses the AnalyticsRepository boundary, and I confirmed the sole non-test implementation scans only three columns (internal/adapters/storage/postgres/analytics_store.go:96-98). The rule is genuinely written twice: acceptance criterion 1's own grep, `git grep -nE 'SpendCents\) / float64' -- internal/ | grep -v _test`, returns exactly the two lines the finding names (campaigns_analytics.go:91 and internal/domain/inventory/tuning.go:235), so the criterion is calibrated against a real baseline of 2 and a real target of 1. Consumer enumeration also holds when widened to test files: no mock or stub populates the fields either, so no implementation anywhere makes them non-zero.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Nothing material. One presentational note: evidence item 2 quotes its command output with an elision ('...') inside the SQL string; the full sed range does print the quoted lines, so this is abridgement rather than misquotation. Also worth recording for the fixer, though the finding does not overstate it: the handler's substitution of the campaign's current DailySpendCapCents for every historical day means the fill-rate chart is retroactively rewritten whenever a user edits the cap. The finding treats this as a design smell and does not claim it as a bug, which is the correct posture, since no per-day historical cap is persisted anywhere for the fix to use.

basis: The central claim survives and I established it by type comparison rather than by reading the finding's reasoning. Writer: internal/adapters/scheduler/dh_analytics_refresh_steps.go:140-143 marshals `entry.Velocity`, which is dh.CharacterVelocityFields (internal/adapters/clients/dh/types_analytics.go:233-245). Reader: internal/domain/demand/service.go:284-292 unmarshals into the unexported demand.velocityBlobJSON. I diffed the two tag sets field by field: all eight tags the domain mirror declares (median_days_to_sell, sample_size, velocity_change_pct, avg_daily_sales, sell_through_rate_30d, sales_volume_7d, sales_volume_30d, supply_count) do exist on the DH type today, so the mirror is currently accurate — and nothing but that coincidence keeps it so, because the two structs share no Go type and no compile-time relationship. The blobs really do cross the port as opaque *string: internal/domain/demand/repository.go:12-23 passes CardCache/CharacterCache by value, and types.go:15-27 declares the five *string JSON fields. `git grep -nE 'json.Unmarshal' -- internal/domain/demand/ | grep -v _test` returns four sites, so acceptance criterion 1 has a real non-empty baseline to drive to zero. Severity is where this finding overreaches, so I lowered it: the demonstrated consequence is a latent silent-nil on an internal analytics surface if DH renames a wire field, with no current defect and no user-visible effect, which is a low, not a medium.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Two of the five evidence items do not support the claims attached to them. (1) Evidence item 4 says a storage-decoding failure mode 'has leaked all the way into the API response type ... returns the count as a response field.' It has not. demand.CampaignSignalsResponse is the domain SERVICE return type; it carries no JSON tags at all (internal/domain/demand/campaign_signals.go:28-44), and SkippedRows never reaches the wire — the HTTP body is built by toCampaignSignalsDTO into campaignSignalsResponseDTO, whose only fields are computed_at, data_quality and signals (internal/adapters/httpserver/handlers/campaign_signals_handler.go:46-50). The handler's sole use of SkippedRows is a Warn log at campaign_signals_handler.go:36-39. An observability counter on a service return value is defensible design, not a leak, and this item should carry no weight. (2) Evidence item 5 misreads the package doc. internal/domain/demand/types.go:1-6 promises that DH payloads 'are parsed here into domain-local structs so the SCORING LOGIC stays decoupled from the wire format' — and that is exactly what happens: velocityBlobJSON is a domain-local struct and the scoring path consumes signalEntry, not the blob. The doc makes no promise about the repository interface being wire-free, so citing it as an unmet claim is unfair to it. Stripped of both items the finding still stands on items 1-3, but on a narrower base than 'medium' implies.

basis: All four evidence commands reproduce exactly, including the negative one — `git grep -nE '^[^/]*[Tt]ombstoneThreshold' -- 'internal/domain/**/*.go' 'internal/platform/**/*.go'` exits 1 with no output, which is the correct way to evidence an absence under PREAMBLE rule 5. I read both declaration sites in full rather than trusting the grep: internal/adapters/clients/dhprice/provider.go:21 and internal/adapters/storage/postgres/dh_card_tombstone_store.go:10 each declare an unexported `tombstoneThreshold = 3`, and the postgres copy is load-bearing twice (IsTombstoned at :32 and the Count query parameter at :77). I independently confirmed the sharing constraint by reading scripts/check-imports.sh whole: the storage-to-clients rule at line 23 is a `grep -rn` over the entire internal/adapters/storage/ tree, so it is one of the rules that actually works and is untouched by the six-name blind spot in the flat-sibling rule further down the same file. Acceptance criterion 1's grep returns exactly the two declaration lines today, so it has a real baseline; the store test named in criterion 3 exists (internal/adapters/storage/postgres/dh_card_tombstone_store_test.go). Severity low is correctly assigned.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: One overstatement in evidence item 1, which says the constant is 'used to make the same decision in each' package. Only the postgres copy makes the decision: dh_card_tombstone_store.go:32 is the authoritative IsTombstoned predicate and :77 bounds the Count query. The dhprice copy at provider.go:171 only selects which of two log messages to emit ('dh card tombstoned' vs 'dh card lookup failed') and gates nothing. Drift between the two therefore produces a misleading log line, not a wrong tombstone decision — which is consistent with the low severity already assigned, so the conclusion is unaffected. Separately, evidence item 3 says the two packages 'cannot share a constant directly'; strictly, check-imports.sh only forbids storage importing clients, so the reverse direction is not mechanically blocked. It would be an obvious layering inversion and no reviewer would take it, so the finding's conclusion that internal/domain or internal/platform is the only sensible home is right, but the word 'cannot' is stronger than the script enforces.

basis: Every evidence command reproduces, and I re-derived both load-bearing claims by my own route. METHOD COUNT: rather than trust the finding's line-grep, I parsed the package with go/ast and recursively flattened each interface's embedded method set (/tmp/count.go, `go run`). Result: Service = 55 distinct methods, not 54 — CRUDService 15, AnalyticsService 7, ImportService 12, PricingService 12, CertLookupService 2, SnapshotService 3, DHService 3, summing to 54, plus Close() declared on Service itself at internal/domain/inventory/service.go:184. The union is real and is the size the finding describes. ZERO CONSUMERS, checked per interface individually and across the whole tracked tree with no exclusions at all (`git grep -nE '\bNAME\b' -- '*.go'`, tests, mocks and cmd/ included): CRUDService, DHService, CertLookupService and SnapshotService each return exactly three hits and the same three in every case — the declaration in service_interfaces.go, the embedding line in Service, and a `var _ X = (*service)(nil)` compile-time assertion at service.go:371-377. Not one consumer exists for any of the four, so the claim does not merely survive, it survives the widest search I could run. I also verified the reachability caveat that would normally kill a zero-refs claim: these are not dead symbols reached through an exported enclosing function, because an interface type in Go must be named to be depended upon, and the only namings are self-referential. One point the finding understates and I confirmed independently: internal/adapters/scheduler/snapshot_enrich.go:12-15 declares a local SnapshotEnrichService with ProcessPendingSnapshots and RetryFailedSnapshots — a strict two-of-three subset of the published SnapshotService (service_interfaces.go:88-92), whose own doc comment reads '(used by schedulers)'. The scheduler hand-rolled the exact interface that was published for it and left the published one at zero consumers. That is the finding's thesis demonstrated concretely rather than asserted. Severity low is honest: there is no runtime consequence.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Two defects, neither fatal. (1) The title and evidence item 5 say '54-method union'; the true figure is 55. The undercount comes from the counting command targeting service_interfaces.go alone, which cannot see Close() at service.go:184. Task 14 should use 55 — and should note that ARCH-004's corrected count now coincides numerically with SIZE-001's 55-method PurchaseRepository. That is a coincidence between a service interface and a repository interface on opposite sides of the port, not evidence of duplication; per ADJUDICATIONS.md these remain two findings, and I did not treat either as grounds against the other. (2) Acceptance criterion 2 is defective. 'No adapter declares a comment matching "subset of inventory.Service"' is a comment-text grep satisfiable by rewording two comments without changing a single dependency, and it also contradicts the finding's own fix branch (b), which explicitly accepts the union as the real contract and would leave both local subsets standing. A ticket should drop or restate that criterion. It is not fatal because criterion 1 — every interface in service_interfaces.go has at least one non-test consumer — is a genuine outcome-stated end state, mechanically checkable by one grep per name, and satisfiable by either fix branch, which together with the build/test and unmodified-handler-test gates is enough for a fixer to prove the change correct.

basis: Both evidence commands reproduce and the narrow factual claim is exactly right. Widening the search to include test files, `git grep -nE '\bWithHTTPStatus\b' -- 'internal/**/*.go' 'cmd/**/*.go'` shows every call site is in internal/domain/errors/errors_test.go (lines 161, 174, 266, 290, 297, 308); the only non-test hits are the declaration at errors.go:165 and two doc comments. HTTPStatus() has exactly the one non-test reader at internal/platform/resilience/retry.go:142. I answered the runtime checks the finding's exclusions declare it did not run: AppError is never embedded (the only non-test uses outside its own package are `var appErr *errors.AppError` type-assertion targets at campaigns_finance.go:266 and retry.go:91,135), no interface anywhere declares a WithHTTPStatus method, and there is no reflection or string-keyed route to the setter. Confidence 'suspected' and category 'dead-code' are correctly assigned, and the routing is correct — this belongs to the dead-code lens. I am marking it not ticketable on the LENS-BRIEF section 7 test rather than on its truth: its first acceptance criterion, 'Dead-code lens returns a verdict on WithHTTPStatus with all nine runtime checks answered', is an instruction to another audit lens, not something a fixer can prove; the second is conditional on a removal decision the finding deliberately does not make. A 'suspected' pointer is by construction recorded and not ticketed.
what_the_finding_got_wrong: Nothing wrong, but it stops one step short of a fact that strengthens it and that the dead-code lens will need. AppError.HTTPStatusCode is assigned in exactly one place in all non-test code — inside WithHTTPStatus itself (errors.go:167 and :169) — and the alternative population path HTTPStatus() consults, Context["http_status"] (errors.go:102), is set only in errors_test.go. Since WithHTTPStatus has no non-test caller, neither source is ever populated in production, so HTTPStatus() can only return 0 at runtime and the retry-policy branch at retry.go:142-143 that reads it is inert. That makes the reader dead too, not just the setter, which enlarges the removal candidate beyond what the finding scopes. I am recording this rather than inflating the finding on it, since ARCH-005 does not claim it.
